perFinding.title: PhusdMinterRepoint ABI drift — 7-field decode + setMaxMintPerDay vs live 4-field minter with no cap setter; preview reverts before any mutation

candidatesConsidered.ki: External vault/yield strategy behavior (out of scope)
candidatesConsidered.argument: Root cause is the in-scope MIGRATION SCRIPT (PhusdMinterRepoint.s.sol) ABI-decoding a StablecoinConfig shape and calling a setter that the LIVE deployed phUSD minter (in-scope Phoenix code, PhusdStableMinter) does not expose. This is script-vs-deployed-contract VERSION DRIFT, not the behaviour of an external vault. The phUSD minter is not the 'external vault' the KI refers to.

candidatesConsidered.ki: Admin trust assumptions for registering stablecoins, setting rates (operational risk)
candidatesConsidered.argument: Not an admin-trust/reckless-admin class. The script reverts at preview regardless of operator competence; a non-malicious operator following the documented forge procedure cannot complete the repoint, and is left with the minter permanently pointed at the evacuated old strategies. Per CLAUDE.md Law 3 this is a NON-OBVIOUS footgun (silent inability to complete) — explicitly IN SCOPE, not suppressed as admin trust.

candidatesConsidered.ki: Minting rights requirements for PhlimboEA and PhusdStableMinter (configuration, not bug)
candidatesConsidered.argument: That KI covers the operational REQUIREMENT to grant minting rights as a config step. This finding is an ABI/field-count decode mismatch + a call to a non-existent cap setter that aborts the whole repoint — a code/integration bug, not a missing-config-grant.

perFinding.title: story-062 pause coupling — live original staker left contract-globally paused with no break-glass unpauser if the suite halts after deploy/leg1
perFinding.knownIssueVerdict: NOT a known issue — KEEP (Law-3 footgun, not admin-trust)

candidatesConsidered.argument: The owner pausing the live staker as a deliberate migration step is the EXPECTED/trusted action (obvious, Law-3-trusted). But the NON-OBVIOUS consequence — that unpause is reachable ONLY through a fully-successful PostMigrationCleanup, so a mid-suite halt strands the live staker AND the un-migrated USDe pool paused with no break-glass — is precisely the surprise a competent non-malicious owner would not anticipate. Per CLAUDE.md Law 3, a non-obvious owner footgun that unknowingly causes a DoS is IN SCOPE as an operational hazard, NOT suppressed. Confirmed: keep, with safe-config guidance (add a standalone owner break-glass unpause path independent of cleanup completion).

perFinding.title: story-062 cleanup catch-path silently SKIPS pauser restoration — live staker unpaused but left with deployer EOA as pauser instead of the recorded original pauser

candidatesConsidered.ki: Dual-unpause mechanism - both owner AND pauser can unpause (intentional redundancy)
candidatesConsidered.argument: That KI is about who may UNPAUSE being intentionally redundant. This finding is about the wrong ADDRESS being installed as pauser on a degraded (missing-deployments-JSON) catch-path, silently leaving a deployer EOA holding the pauser role on the live staker — a state-handling footgun, not the intended dual-unpause design.

Non-obvious: the operator believes cleanup restored the original pauser (the happy-path asserts it), but the try/catch degrade-path silently substitutes the deployer EOA. Surprise => Law-3 footgun, in scope.

perFinding.title: PhusdMinterRepoint Phase B re-seeds V2 with the below-par recovered amount, no >= principal solvency floor — pre-existing autopool shortfall silently carried into V2
perFinding.knownIssueVerdict: NOT a known issue — KEEP (contingent on DEDUP-13-001)

candidatesConsidered.ki: External vault/yield strategy behavior (out of scope)
candidatesConsidered.argument: The shortfall ORIGINATES in the autopool (which is external), but the FINDING is that the in-scope script's Phase B reseed enforces NO solvency floor on the recovered amount, silently propagating any shortfall into the new V2 position rather than reverting/flagging. The defect is the missing script-level invariant, not the external vault's behaviour. Borderline-adjacent to the KI; resolved KEEP because the actionable root cause is in-scope script code.
